description: Experience the vibrant flavors of a classic Chinese Hot and Sour Soup, a comforting bowl bursting with savory umami, tangy vinegar, and a kick of chili. This authentic recipe balances textures from silken tofu, wood ear mushrooms, and shredded pork, creating a truly satisfying culinary journey. Perfect for a chilly evening or a flavorful starter to any meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Shred the pork loin finely. Drain and slice tofu into thin strips. Rehydrate dried wood ear and shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 20-30 minutes, then squeeze dry, trim tough stems, and slice thinly. Reserve the shiitake soaking liquid if desired. Prepare your cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with cold water until smooth.

instructions.title: Cook the Pork
instructions.text: In a large pot or wok, add a tablespoon of cooking oil over medium-high heat. Add the shredded pork and stir-fry until it is cooked through and lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove the pork from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Simmer the Broth and Vegetables
instructions.text: Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into the pot. Add the sliced wood ear mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, and julienned bamboo shoots. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. If using, add the reserved shiitake soaking liquid.

instructions.title: Add Seasonings and Tofu
instructions.text: Stir in the Chinkiang black vinegar, soy sauce, and white pepper. Add the sliced tofu and the cooked pork back into the pot. Let it simmer gently for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Taste and adjust seasonings if necessary, adding more vinegar or soy sauce to your preference.

instructions.title: Thicken the Soup
instructions.text: Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir to recombine, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream while continuously stirring. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. If it becomes too thick, add a little more broth or water.

instructions.title: Finish with Egg and Garnish
instructions.text: Once the soup is thickened, reduce the heat to low. Slowly pour the beaten eggs into the soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction to create delicate 'egg flowers'. Remove from heat immediately. Drizzle with sesame oil and chili oil. Garnish generously with sliced green onions before serving hot.

tips: For an authentic sour kick, use Chinkiang black vinegar. Adjust the amount to your preference, starting with less and adding more.
To get beautiful 'egg flowers', ensure the soup is simmering gently, then pour the beaten egg slowly in a thin stream while stirring the soup gently in one direction.
Rehydrated dried shiitake mushrooms add deep umami; always reserve and use the strained soaking liquid as part of your broth for extra flavor.
article:
Hot and Sour Soup: A Culinary Journey into Chinese Comfort

The world of Chinese cuisine is vast and varied, brimming with dishes that tantalize the taste buds and warm the soul. Among its most beloved liquid offerings, Hot and Sour Soup stands out as a true masterpiece. This iconic soup, celebrated for its unique balance of fiery spice and tangy zest, offers a complex flavor profile that is both comforting and invigorating. It’s a staple on Chinese restaurant menus worldwide, but imagine creating this restaurant-quality dish in your own kitchen! Mastering a homemade Hot and Sour Soup recipe is incredibly rewarding, allowing you to customize its heat, sourness, and texture to your exact preference.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

At its heart, Hot and Sour Soup is a symphony of flavors and textures. Originating from Sichuan or Hunan provinces in China, where spicy and sour elements are prominent in the local cuisine, it has since become a popular dish across various Chinese culinary traditions. The soup is characterized by its signature "hot" (spicy) kick, typically from white pepper and sometimes chili oil, and its "sour" tang, derived primarily from vinegar. Beyond these defining characteristics, it boasts a savory depth from broth, soy sauce, and often umami-rich mushrooms, complemented by a subtle sweetness and a wonderfully thick, velvety texture.

Common ingredients found in Hot and Sour Soup include thinly sliced pork or tofu, rehydrated dried shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and sometimes lily flowers. A whisked egg is often swirled in at the end to create delicate, silken strands, adding to its visual appeal and mouthfeel. The soup is thickened with a cornstarch slurry, giving it that characteristic body that clings to the spoon and delivers a satisfying warmth with every slurp.

## Ingredients You Need

Every great Hot and Sour Soup recipe starts with the right foundation and a selection of fresh, high-quality ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather for an authentic and delicious bowl:

*   **For the Soup Base:**
    *   6 cups chicken or vegetable broth (low sodium preferred)
    *   2 tablespoons soy sauce (light or regular)
    *   2 tablespoons rice vinegar (or Chinkiang black vinegar for a deeper flavor)
    *   1-2 tablespoons white pepper (essential for the "hot" element)
    *   1 teaspoon sesame oil
    *   1 teaspoon sugar (optional, to balance flavors)
    *   Chili oil to taste (optional, for extra heat)
*   **Solid Ingredients:**
    *   4 oz lean pork loin or firm tofu, thinly sliced into matchsticks
    *   4-5 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated, stems removed, sliced
    *   1/4 cup dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated, sliced (or fresh, if available)
    *   1/2 cup canned bamboo shoots, drained and julienned
    *   2 tablespoons dried lily flowers (optional, rehydrated, knotted)
*   **Thickener and Egg:**
    *   2 tablespoons cornstarch
    *   4 tablespoons cold water (for slurry)
    *   1 large egg, whisked
*   **Garnish (Optional):**
    *   2 scallions, green parts thinly sliced
    *   Fresh cilantro, chopped

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Following this Hot and Sour Soup recipe step-by-step will ensure a delicious outcome, even for first-time makers. Precision and timing are key to achieving the perfect balance of flavors and textures.

1.  **Prepare Ingredients:** If using dried mushrooms and lily flowers, soak them in hot water for at least 30 minutes until soft. Drain, squeeze out excess water, remove shiitake stems, and slice all mushrooms and lily flowers (tie lily flowers into knots if desired). Slice pork or tofu into thin matchsticks. Prepare your cornstarch slurry by whisking cornstarch with cold water in a small bowl. Whisk the egg in another small bowl.
2.  **Cook Solids:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring the broth to a simmer over medium heat. Add the sliced pork (or tofu), shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and lily flowers (if using). Bring the soup back to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the pork is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
3.  **Season the Soup:** Stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, white pepper, sesame oil, and sugar (if using). Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning. This is where you can personalize the "hot" and "sour" elements. Add more white pepper for heat, or more vinegar for tanginess, according to your preference.
4.  **Thicken the Soup:** Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir to recombine it, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Continue to stir until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. This usually takes about 1-2 minutes. If it's too thick, add a little more broth or water.
5.  **Add the Egg:** Once the soup is thickened, reduce the heat to low. Slowly pour the whisked egg into the soup in a thin, continuous stream while gently stirring the soup in one direction with chopsticks or a fork. This creates delicate, feathery egg ribbons. Stop stirring once all the egg is incorporated and has cooked into strands, about 30 seconds.
6.  **Final Touches & Serve:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in a dash of chili oil if you desire extra heat. Ladle the Hot and Sour Soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh scallions and cilantro, if using, and serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

To elevate your Hot and Sour Soup recipe from good to extraordinary, consider these expert tips:

*   **Quality Broth Matters:** A good quality chicken or vegetable broth forms the backbone of your soup. Homemade broth will always yield the best flavor, but a good store-bought low-sodium option works well.
*   **Don't Be Shy with White Pepper and Vinegar:** These are the defining "hot" and "sour" components. Start with the suggested amounts, but don't hesitate to add more to taste. White pepper provides a unique warmth that differs from chili heat.
*   **Chinkiang Black Vinegar:** While regular rice vinegar works, Chinkiang black vinegar offers a more complex, slightly malty, and deeper sour flavor that is characteristic of many authentic Chinese dishes. It’s worth seeking out.
*   **Rehydrate Dried Ingredients Properly:** Ensure dried shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, and lily flowers are fully rehydrated and squeezed dry before adding. This maximizes their flavor and texture.
*   **Achieving Silky Egg Strands:** The key is to pour the whisked egg slowly into a gently simmering (not boiling) soup while stirring in one direction. This prevents the egg from clumping and creates beautiful, delicate ribbons.
*   **Adjust to Taste:** The beauty of making your own Hot and Sour Soup recipe is the ability to customize. Taste and adjust the soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper, and chili oil until it perfectly suits your palate.

## Serving Suggestions

Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in several ways:

*   **As an Appetizer:** It makes a fantastic starter for any Chinese meal, whetting the appetite with its vibrant flavors.
*   **Part of a Dim Sum Spread:** Pair it with dumplings, spring rolls, and other small bites for a delightful spread.
*   **Alongside Main Dishes:** Serve it alongside classic Chinese dishes like stir-fries, fried rice, or noodle dishes to complete the meal. Its bold flavors complement milder mains beautifully.
*   **Light Lunch:** A large bowl of Hot and Sour Soup can be a satisfying and warming meal in itself, especially on a chilly day.
*   **Garnishes:** Don't forget the fresh garnishes! A sprinkle of chopped scallions and cilantro adds a burst of freshness and color. A drizzle of extra chili oil can provide an additional kick for spice lovers.

## Variations and Substitutions

The versatility of a Hot and Sour Soup recipe means it can be adapted to suit various dietary needs and preferences.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Easily make this soup vegetarian or vegan by using vegetable broth, firm tofu instead of pork, and omitting the egg. For a vegan version, ensure your chili oil doesn't contain animal products.
*   **Different Meats:** Instead of pork, you can use thinly sliced chicken breast or shrimp. Add shrimp towards the end of the cooking process as they cook quickly.
*   **Mushroom Variety:** Experiment with other mushrooms like enoki or oyster mushrooms for added texture and flavor.
*   **Spice Level:** Control the heat by adjusting the amount of white pepper and chili oil. For those who like it extra fiery, a pinch of dried red chili flakes can be added during the simmering stage.
*   **Sourness:** If you prefer it extra tangy, feel free to add another splash of vinegar at the very end, just before serving.

Armed with this comprehensive guide, you're ready to create a memorable Hot and Sour Soup recipe right in your own kitchen. This flavorful and comforting soup is a testament to the rich culinary traditions of China, and now, you can bring that warmth and zest to your own dining table. Enjoy the process of crafting this beloved dish, and savor every spoonful!
